audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 acquired-business revenue was $2.795 billion, 58.1% of the $4.807 billion revenue increase; first-half 2026 acquired-business revenue was $1.730 billion, 39.1% of the $4.425 billion increase; 2025 acquisition cash spending was $3.052 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical acquisition-supported growth informs the 8%-10% growth assumptions, while acquisition cash outlays are excluded from OE
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 was primarily due to increased demand for our services, as well as approximately $1.87 billion in revenues attributable to acquired businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: This does not prove that forecast growth must be purchased, but it demonstrates that a large portion of recent reported growth came from acquisitions. Because recurring acquisition spending exceeded twice the $1.468 billion OE anchor in 2025, omitting any acquisition allowance while extrapolating acquired growth is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic from acquired OE growth for 2023-2026 and rerun the valuation using either organic growth alone or an explicit recurring acquisition cash allowance.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 fair-value liability of $814.402 million equals $5.28 per share and 2.90% of base equity value; the $921.4 million maximum equals $5.97 per share and 3.28% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The expected cash-settled obligation should reduce the equity bridge unless its economic cost is already captured in OE; stock settlement instead affects shares
audit_findings.evidence: All of Quanta’s outstanding contingent consideration liabilities are each subject to a maximum payment amount, and the aggregate maximum payment amount of these liabilities for acquisitions completed prior to December 31, 2025 totaled $ 713.0 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but its filed scale does not change the conclusion. Even deducting the full maximum would reduce base value from $182.06 to about $176.09 per share and leave it far below the $620.06 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $814.402 million latest fair value by acquisition and rerun the bridge with expected cash settlement deducted and expected stock settlement added to shares, without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Anchor earnings depend on unapproved claims revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: Unapproved change-order and claims revenue declined from $983.6 million at December 2025 to $411.1 million at June 2026, a $572.5 million or 58.2% reduction; embedded profit is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unrecoverable profit recognized in 2025 would overstate the OE anchor and every projected OE amount derived from it
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, Quanta had recognized revenues of $ 983.6 million and $ 733.6 million related to unapproved change orders and claims included as contract price adjustments primarily in “Contract assets” in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing materially reduces the concern because customer approval of the large Canadian-project balance was the largest component of the decline. However, $411.1 million remains unapproved, and the record does not disclose the profit included in either the year-end or remaining balance, subsequent cash collection, or how the OE construction treated it. Materiality therefore cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level gross profit embedded in the December 2025 and June 2026 balances, subsequent approvals and cash collections, and rerun the anchor excluding any profit that fails the approval-and-collection test.

audit_findings.title: Silverado wildfire exposure is unreserved and unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured loss, deductible, defense cost or coverage shortfall would reduce OE when incurred or require an equity-bridge deduction
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, Quanta had not recorded an accrual with respect to this matter, and Quanta is currently unable to reasonably estimate a range of reasonably possible loss, if any, because there are a number of unknown facts and legal considerations that may impact the amount of any potential liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing provides favorable new evidence: management says a material loss is not probable and believes insurance is adequate above the applicable deductible. Nevertheless, no case-specific deductible, loss range, policy limit or coverage analysis is supplied, so the record cannot establish the potential valuation effect or demonstrate that it is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Silverado-specific deductible, policy limits and exclusions, defense-cost treatment, indemnification terms and updated litigation posture; rerun only if a probable or probability-weighted uninsured exposure can be supported.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earnouts can create dilution outside the share ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: As a conservative illustration, stock-settling the entire $921.4 million maximum at $620.06 would issue about 1.486 million shares, 0.96% of the 154.321 million share denominator; actual contractual stock-settlement percentages are substantially lower
audit_findings.mechanism: Stock-settled earnouts increase fully diluted shares; cash-settled amounts instead reduce the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: To the extent payable, Quanta, at its sole discretion, can pay 15 % of any such contingent consideration amount in Quanta common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: Potential dilution outside the supplied share ceiling is demonstrated, but even an illustration assuming 100% stock settlement—more than the contracts permit—would reduce the denominator-based value by less than 1%, about $1.93 per share in the bull case. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain expected earnout payments, settlement formulas and management's cash-versus-stock elections; add expected shares and deduct expected cash obligations without double counting finding 2.

audit_findings.title: Not all consolidated cash is distributable to common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 joint-venture cash of $84.244 million plus captive-insurance cash of $9.701 million totals $93.945 million, equal to $0.61 per share and 0.33% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unavailable cash was included in the $506.431 million equity-bridge cash add-back
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents held by joint ventures, which are either consolidated or proportionately consolidated, are available to support joint venture operations, but Quanta cannot utilize those assets to support its other operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: only $412.486 million of consolidated cash was outside joint ventures and the captive insurer. Removing the $93.945 million unavailable portion would reduce base value from $182.06 to about $181.45 per share and buy-below value by about $0.43, which cannot change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge using $412.486 million of cash before separately testing that balance for any other restrictions or operating minimums.
